name: Reverse Curl
description: The reverse curl is a curl variation using an overhand (pronated) grip rather than the standard underhand (supinated) grip. This grip change mechanically disadvantages the biceps brachii while placing the brachioradialis and brachialis as the primary movers. It is an important supplementary exercise for building forearm and outer arm thickness and improving wrist and elbow joint resilience.

execution.starting_position: Stand upright holding a barbell (or dumbbells) with an overhand (pronated) grip, hands shoulder-width apart. Arms are fully extended, bar at thigh level.
execution.setup_instructions: Use a straight barbell, EZ-curl bar, or dumbbells. The load will be significantly lower than a standard curl due to the grip change.
steps: Step 1: Hold the bar with a pronated (overhand) grip, hands shoulder-width apart. Stand tall, upper arms at the sides.
Step 2: Brace the core and keep the upper arms stationary.
Step 3: Exhale and curl the bar upward to shoulder level, maintaining the overhand grip throughout.
Step 4: Hold briefly at the top, then inhale and lower the bar back to the starting position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the curl; inhale on the return.
common_mistakes: Letting the wrists collapse into flexion during the curl — keep wrists neutral or slightly extended
Using the same weight as a supinated curl — reduce load significantly
safety_considerations: If wrist discomfort occurs, switch to an EZ-curl bar which allows a semi-pronated grip
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full arm extension at the bottom; curl to shoulder level at the top.
coaching_cues: Keep wrists flat — do not let them flex toward you during the curl
